content:
maya: FYI bringing up icarus-11b (community 11b) int4 sweep results. quick scorecard pasted below — pinging @owen and @li for routing implications.

maya: ```
SCORES | baseline fp16 | int8 | int4
---|---:|---:|---:
avg-qa-acc | 0.78 | 0.77 | 0.70
summarization-rougeL | 0.56 | 0.55 | 0.48
latency (p50) | 120ms | 95ms | 70ms
cost per 1k tok | $0.88 | $0.62 | $0.29
pass-rate (prod prompts) | 0.94 | 0.92 | 0.81
notes | stable | small degrade on long prompts | notable hallucination spikes >512 tokens
```

maya: Full eval set attached in S3 (s3://redwood-evals/icarus/2025-02-int4). Short summary: int4 looks great on short-context chat workloads but shows quality regressions on multi-turn and long-context summarization. :warning:

owen: looked through the diffs — hallucination clusters correlate with heavy numeric/composite instructions and >600 token context. reproduction snippet in case useful:

owen: ```
PROMPT (repro): "Summarize the quarterly metrics for product X... (700 tokens)
GOLD contains multiple numeric tables
int4 output invents a \"growth by 12%\" line not present in gold
```

li: thanks — did we try hybrid routing by context length? i.e., int4 for <=256 tokens, int8 for 257-800, fp16/hosted fallback for >800 or when numeric ops detected.

maya: not yet on fleet. I ran infra-scale simulations: simple threshold routing reduces unit cost by ~28% vs baseline while keeping overall pass-rate ~0.90 on our prod sample. But we still see a tail of bad failures that product teams will notice.

sasha: product/GTN ask: what's recommendation for default slot in gtn? they want 1) minimal cost impact for free tier and 2) conservative defaults for paid. my suggestion: default to int8 for free tier (balanced), opt-in int4 dev flag for dev orgs, and for paid enable hybrid routing with thresholds and safety fallback.

maya: proposal for rollout steps:
1) rollout int4 to internal dev only (canary) + enable evalbot auto-alerts on cohort drop >5% pass-rate
2) enable hybrid routing gate for GTN paid orgs (<=256 -> int4, 256-800 -> int8, >800 -> fp16/hosted)
3) enable live monitor + automatic fallback to int8/hosted on quality regressions per route

maya: estimate econ impact for GTN paid orgs: ~25-35% token cost savings for chat-heavy apps, 5-10% for long document workloads. Need product buy-in for fallback latency/cost tradeoffs.

evalbot: auto-eval: new int4 baseline vs fp16 on prod-sample-2025-02
evalbot: metrics: delta_pass_rate = -0.13, delta_latency = -42ms, delta_cost = -66%

li: question — can we add a cheap heuristic to detect "numeric-table" prompts and force int8? maybe a fast regex on tokens.

owen: yes, we can ship rule in the router: detect \d{2,} or table delimiters (|, \t) and route to int8. cheap and likely high precision.

sasha: agreed. for GTN docs i'll draft a short guidance: "int4 when short chat, int8 default, route tables->int8, fallback->hosted" — will share shortly.

maya: action items:
- li/owen: implement routing rule + sim in staging (due EOD Fri)
- sasha: draft GTN guidance and default config (due Mon)
- maya: run extended eval with noisy user prompts and share updated scorecard

owen: noted. I'll add a small ablation to check whether per-layer outlier quant helps on numeric ops — might reduce hallucinations without full int8 cost.

li: thanks, will also add a small latency-SLO simulation to ensure fallback doesn't spike p95 beyond 2x.

maya: thanks team. keeping this thread for rollout notes. :thumbsup:
